chapter: Arthur Gibbs, Savoy Ballroom and recording sessions
title: Savoy house bands, Fess Williams and Edgar Sampson
summary: They split the Savoy with Chick Webb in 1927-28, moved to the Colonnades in 1929; Sampson later arranged for Chick, Duke and Fletcher.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: But your band was a little bigger, though.

No, let me see. The dance part, the thing Chick had [John] Trueheart (unintelligible) on guitar, and we had Paul Burnet on banjo, and then the same, trumpet, trombone, two instrumentation saxophone, bass, piano and drums, same as (unintelligible).
Oh, yeah. Yeah. This would be what, about the second year at the Savoy?
This would be in --
Because when that opened up, it was Fess Williams and --
Fess Williams.
-- somebody's Bearcats, may --
Well, that was Duncan Meyers Bearcats.
So you came in after that.

After that. Well, Fess was there when we went there with Arthur Gibbs. (cause) (unintelligible) Chick we were the two house bands, they'd bring 2nd from Arthur Gibbs. (unintelligible) Then we played in bands like there come in town, 25 added attractions, you know, you bring in the band. Then Fess came in with his Savoy band, and he had ten pieces. We only had nine, but that was all right. We didn't pay that no mind. We just had the right
way to do it, and people liked us, and Cecil Scott brought a group in there.
Well, how long did you stay there with Gibbs?
We -- let's see, Arthur Gibbs, we went there in -- Edgar Sampson was in the band too. We went there, opened up there in 1927, played there in '27-28. '29 we went down to the ballroom downtown.
The Colonnade?
Colonnade.
Yeah. Was Sampson arranging in those days?
Sampson was arranging, but he didn't do too much arranging (if he went with) Chick. And from Chick he went with Duke for a while, you know.
Did he?
Yeah, when Duke was -- when Duke first went into the Cotton Club.
Oh, I didn't know Sampson was --
Yeah, and it was with Fletcher too.
